reader: Claude (lead's agent), independent visual read, not ground truth
recorded: 2026-10-25, before any Gemini call and before the pixel digitizer was written
source: data/corpus/files/FOI-1730-1819__1.pdf (TfL FOI-1730-1819, 'Rail Roughness Plots BEG-MIE January 2018'); embedded figure images 1600x598 px viewed natively and as 2x zoomed crops
method: by eye against the printed gridlines and tick labels; pixel row/column positions of gridlines read off the zoomed crops to interpolate between ticks. Header strings transcribed from the text printed inside each figure image.

points.what: global maximum of the 30-100 mm MA Pk-Pk trace (LHR)
global maximum of the 100-300 mm MA Pk-Pk trace (RHR)
LHR roughness spectrum at the 125 mm band (local peak)
LHR roughness spectrum at the 200 mm band (local dip before the 125 mm peak)
RHR roughness spectrum at the 200 mm band (local peak)
RHR roughness spectrum at the 250 mm band (local dip before the 200 mm peak)

observations_not_scored: Each figure has two panels: (top) moving-average peak-to-peak roughness in the caption's wavelength band vs Position (m); (bottom) a roughness spectrum, dB rel 1 µm RMS vs third-octave wavelength band 2000 mm to 3.15 mm.
The bottom spectrum looks the same in Figures 1 and 2 (LHR) and in Figures 3 and 4 (RHR): one spectrum per rail, repeated.
The roughest stretch on both rails starts abruptly near 720-725 m and is highest to about 890-900 m; the LHR stays above the 10 µm line in the 30-100 mm band to about 1,230 m.
Three unlabelled straight lines (grey, magenta, olive) on each spectrum and pink vertical lines on each position panel have no legend in the PDF; not identified.
LHR and RHR are not expanded in the PDF (conventionally left-hand / right-hand rail).
